correctness.rationale: For all m>=3,n>=5, the proof carefully takes ordinary polyhedral Hom(C_m,C_n) with cells of coordinate size one or two and isolated monotone maps excluded from H1. The established Čukić–Kozlov circle-or-point component theorem provides rank-one H1 on components indexed by winding w and, for even n, first-color parity p. Their contractible-patch cover has nerve the target-color +2 cycle. Evaluation e0 maps a nerve generator along each two-edge target arc: degree two for odd n and degree one for even n. The proof compares all e_j by cellwise homotopies; target reflection multiplies evaluation degree by -1 while source reflections preserve it. Injectivity of evaluation on each circle component then fixes the SIGN of the integral generator, yielding exactly t times the permutation w->st w and parity shift p->p+k+ell. The two separate reflections act with opposing signs on the same component permutation, forcing all positive-degree rational quotient homology to vanish by semisimple finite-group coinvariants. I independently built 1-skeleta of actual Hom graph maps for (m,n)=(6,5),(7,5),(8,5),(8,6),(10,6), computed evaluation windings around every fundamental graph cycle by integer spanning-tree cocycles, and obtained image index 2 for all nontrivial odd-n components and 1 for even-n components. The family proof is analytical, not deduced from these samples. Code of full group-element finite signed-cubical verifier was inspected.

value.rationale: The natural commuting source/target D_m x D_n action has an integral signed permutation module more informative than circle component counts. Distinguishing source and target reflection signs, parity-sensitive evaluation subgroup, and rational acyclicity of the full group quotient resolves an intrinsic equivariant extension of classical Hom(C_m,C_n) classification for two unbounded parameters. It neither relabels an old Betti number nor requires a new equivariant homotopy classification.
